title: Graceful-degradation non-blocking hotpatch for multi-tenant TTFT regressions
creator: Michael Huang
description:
Summary: Several customers in Hosted and Dedicated tiers reported sudden TTFT regressions and reduced tokens/sec on short-chat workloads after last scheduler commit. This ticket tracks an emergency, minimally-invasive hotpatch that enables graceful degradation by switching to a non-blocking streaming path and adaptive batch throttling when per-worker batching latency exceeds thresholds. Goal is to restore first-token latency and tokens/sec for affected traffic without full scheduler rollback.

Context: On 2026-03-09 we rolled scheduler v2.3.1 which introduced a new windowed batching heuristic. In production we observed head-of-line blocking when traffic mixes short priming calls and long-context completions; the window heuristic increased batching wait time for short requests, inflating TTFT by 150-600ms for affected tenants. The degradation was intermittent across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments depending on request patterns and kernel availability.

High-level approach: implement a hotpatch control flag (adaptive_nonblocking_mode) that: 1) monitors per-worker batch wait time and estimated wait-to-compute ratio; 2) if the ratio crosses a safety threshold, routes short requests to the non-blocking streaming execution path (bypassing synchronous batching); 3) applies a soft limit on batch fill time (circuit-breaker style) and enforces per-tenant priority smoothing to avoid starvation. This avoids full scheduler rollback and keeps throughput for long-running requests while restoring TTFT for latency-sensitive short calls.
root_cause: Regression introduced by windowed batching heuristic in scheduler v2.3.1: batching wait timers were scaled using a global percentile derived from multi-tenant latency signals which did not account for skewed short-request bursts. This caused long waits before flush for small requests and led to head-of-line blocking when multiplexed on the same worker. Kernel warmstart interactions amplified the effect on quantized models running on Dedicated pools.
mitigations: Enable adaptive_nonblocking_mode toggle with default OFF for all regions
Short-circuit flush for requests with expected token_count <= 16 when measured wait > 40ms
Per-tenant soft priority smoothing to avoid priority inversion
Increase scheduler probe frequency in Dedicated canaries for 24h post-deploy
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy hotpatch to staging; run canary suite against short/long mixed workloads (see testing_notes)
2) Canary on Dedicated pool alpha-1 (10% traffic) for 2h; monitor TTFT and tokens/sec dashboards
3) If green, promote to Hosted canary (5% traffic) for 2h while observing customer-specific tenants that reported issues
4) Full rollout to Hosted + Dedicated + Private control plane flag flip after 24h of stable metrics; offer Private customers opt-in and patches for on-prem agents
5) Post-rollout: revert toggle after upstream scheduler fix merged or keep toggle as safety fallback depending on regression root-cause fix ETA
testing_notes: Synthetic mixed-workload replay (concurrency 200, 60% short chat <=16 tokens, 40% long completions) — compare baseline scheduler v2.3.0 vs patched v2.3.1+toggle
Load tests include kernel heterogeneity: FLOAT16, INT8-quantized, and CPU fallback nodes
A/B traffic for affected enterprise tenant 'Skyboard' with telemetry hooks enabled to trace per-request batching path
Automated e2e test added: ensure streaming path has no token-loss under backpressure (see PR comments)
acceptance_criteria: TTFT median for short-chat workloads reduced to within 15% of pre-regression baseline across Hosted and Dedicated canaries
Tokens/sec throughput for mixed workload recovers to within 95% of baseline on Dedicated pools
No increase in error rate or OOMs attributable to the non-blocking path during 48h post-rollout
Private on-prem customers can opt-in and receive a backported agent with identical toggle semantics

2026-03-12 Carlos Gomez (SRE): Canary run on staging looks good; TTFT for short requests down from +420ms to +30ms vs baseline. Observed 3% increase in small kernel invocations; memory stable. Recommend canary on Dedicated alpha-1.

2026-03-13 Eva Martinez (PM): Customer 'Skyboard' validated improved responsiveness in dev environment. They requested opt-in for Private once patch is available. Added to customer_communications backlog.
